audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Elijah ascent and Elisha succession narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Gilgal-Bethel-Jericho-Jordan itinerary, sons of prophets, Elijah's ascent, double-portion request, mantle/Jordan sign, Jericho water healing, and bears episode.

verses.restored: When YHWH was about to take Elijah up in storm-wind to heavens, Elijah and Elisha went from Gilgal.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when the LORD would take up Elijah into heaven by a whirlwind, that Elijah went with Elisha from Gilgal.

verses.restored: Elijah said to Elisha, Stay here, please, for YHWH has sent me to Bethel. Elisha said, As YHWH lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. So they went down to Bethel.

familiar.text: And Elijah said unto Elisha, Tarry here, I pray thee; for the LORD hath sent me to Bethel. And Elisha said unto him, As the LORD liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. So they went down to Bethel.

verses.restored: Sons of prophets at Bethel came to Elisha and said, Do you know that today YHWH is taking your master from over your head? He said, I also know; be silent.

familiar.text: And the sons of the prophets that were at Bethel came forth to Elisha, and said unto him, Knowest thou that the LORD will take away thy master from thy head to day? And he said, Yea, I know it; hold ye your peace.

verses.restored: Elijah said, Elisha, stay here, please, for YHWH has sent me to Jericho. He said, As YHWH lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. So they came to Jericho.

familiar.text: And Elijah said unto him, Elisha, tarry here, I pray thee; for the LORD hath sent me to Jericho. And he said, As the LORD liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. So they came to Jericho.

verses.restored: Sons of prophets at Jericho came to Elisha and said, Do you know that today YHWH is taking your master from over your head? He said, I also know; be silent.

familiar.text: And the sons of the prophets that were at Jericho came to Elisha, and said unto him, Knowest thou that the LORD will take away thy master from thy head to day? And he answered, Yea, I know it; hold ye your peace.

verses.restored: Elijah said, Stay here, please, for YHWH has sent me to Jordan. He said, As YHWH lives and as your soul lives, I will not leave you. So the two of them went.

familiar.text: And Elijah said unto him, Tarry, I pray thee, here; for the LORD hath sent me to Jordan. And he said, As the LORD liveth, and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee. And they two went on.

verses.restored: Fifty men from sons of prophets went and stood opposite at a distance, while the two stood by Jordan.

familiar.text: And fifty men of the sons of the prophets went, and stood to view afar off: and they two stood by Jordan.

verses.restored: Elijah took his mantle, rolled it, struck waters, and they divided here and there; the two crossed on dry ground.

familiar.text: And Elijah took his mantle, and wrapped it together, and smote the waters, and they were divided hither and thither, so that they two went over on dry ground.

verses.restored: When they crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, Ask what I shall do for you before I am taken from you. Elisha said, Let a double portion of your spirit be upon me.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when they were gone over, that Elijah said unto Elisha, Ask what I shall do for thee, before I be taken away from thee. And Elisha said, I pray thee, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me.

verses.restored: He said, You have asked a hard thing. If you see me being taken from you, it shall be so; if not, it shall not be.

familiar.text: And he said, Thou hast asked a hard thing: nevertheless, if thou see me when I am taken from thee, it shall be so unto thee; but if not, it shall not be so.

verses.restored: As they were walking and speaking, look, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them, and Elijah went up in storm-wind to heavens.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as they still went on, and talked, that, behold, there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and parted them both asunder; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.

verses.restored: Elisha was seeing and cried, My father, my father! Chariot of Israel and its horsemen! He saw him no more. He grasped his clothes and tore them in two pieces.

familiar.text: And Elisha saw it, and he cried, My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof. And he saw him no more: and he took hold of his own clothes, and rent them in two pieces.

verses.restored: He lifted Elijah's mantle that had fallen from upon him and returned and stood on bank of Jordan.

familiar.text: He took up also the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and went back, and stood by the bank of Jordan;

verses.restored: He took Elijah's mantle that had fallen and struck waters, saying, Where is YHWH, Divine of Elijah? He struck waters, and they divided here and there, and Elisha crossed.

familiar.text: And he took the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and smote the waters, and said, Where is the LORD God of Elijah? and when he also had smitten the waters, they parted hither and thither: and Elisha went over.

verses.restored: Sons of prophets at Jericho saw him opposite and said, Spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha. They came to meet him and bowed to ground before him.

familiar.text: And when the sons of the prophets which were to view at Jericho saw him, they said, The spirit of Elijah doth rest on Elisha. And they came to meet him, and bowed themselves to the ground before him.

verses.restored: They said, Look, there are with your servants fifty strong men; let them go seek your master, lest Spirit of YHWH lifted him and cast him on some mountain or valley. He said, Do not send.

familiar.text: And they said unto him, Behold now, there be with thy servants fifty strong men; let them go, we pray thee, and seek thy master: lest peradventure the Spirit of the LORD hath taken him up, and cast him upon some mountain, or into some valley. And he said, Ye shall not send.

verses.restored: They pressed him until he was ashamed, and he said, Send. They sent fifty men, searched three days, and did not find him.

familiar.text: And when they urged him till he was ashamed, he said, Send. They sent therefore fifty men; and they sought three days, but found him not.

verses.restored: They returned to him while he stayed at Jericho, and he said, Did I not say to you, Do not go?

familiar.text: And when they came again to him, (for he tarried at Jericho,) he said unto them, Did I not say unto you, Go not?

verses.restored: Men of city said to Elisha, Look, dwelling of city is good, as my lord sees, but waters are bad and land miscarries/bereaves.

familiar.text: And the men of the city said unto Elisha, Behold, I pray thee, the situation of this city is pleasant, as my lord seeth: but the water is naught, and the ground barren.

verses.restored: He said, Bring me a new bowl and put salt in it. They brought it to him.

familiar.text: And he said, Bring me a new cruse, and put salt therein. And they brought it to him.

verses.restored: He went out to spring of waters, threw salt there, and said, Thus says YHWH: I have healed these waters; no more shall death or miscarriage/bereavement come from there.

familiar.text: And he went forth unto the spring of the waters, and cast the salt in there, and said, Thus saith the LORD, I have healed these waters; there shall not be from thence any more death or barren land.

verses.restored: Waters were healed to this day, according to word of Elisha that he spoke.

familiar.text: So the waters were healed unto this day, according to the saying of Elisha which he spake.

verses.restored: He went up from there to Bethel. As he was going up by road, small youths came out from city and mocked him, saying, Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!

familiar.text: And he went up from thence unto Bethel: and as he was going up by the way, there came forth little children out of the city, and mocked him, and said unto him, Go up, thou bald head; go up, thou bald head.

verses.restored: He turned behind him, saw them, and cursed them in name of YHWH. Two female bears came out from forest and tore forty-two of the youths.

familiar.text: And he turned back, and looked on them, and cursed them in the name of the LORD. And there came forth two she bears out of the wood, and tare forty and two children of them.

verses.restored: He went from there to Mount Carmel, and from there returned to Samaria.

familiar.text: And he went from thence to mount Carmel, and from thence he returned to Samaria.

translation_notes: Elisha's refusal to leave Elijah is fidelity at a death/succession threshold, not permission to deny another person's boundaries in ordinary relationships.
The sons of prophets know loss is coming; Elisha's repeated 'be silent' may mark grief too raw for public processing.
The double portion evokes firstborn inheritance language and succession responsibility, not a request to be twice as impressive.
Elijah's ascent is visionary succession narrative; it should not be used to deny death, grief, or burial for others.
Jericho's water healing addresses public health, fertility of land, and communal survival; miracle language must not replace environmental responsibility or medical care.
The bears episode is morally dangerous. Mockery does not justify child harm, animal attack, cursing children, or violent retaliation by spiritual leaders.
The term often rendered 'boys' or 'youths' is debated, but any age reading requires anti-child-harm safeguards.
safety_note: Do not use 2 Kings 2 to justify cursing children, violence for mockery, denial of grief, leader cult succession, or miracle claims that replace public-health action. Center faithful succession, honest mourning, healed water, and the absolute refusal to make the bears episode a model for spiritual authority.
